A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BMIA research despite the changed title and substantial expansion. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support comparison, including matching material moved from the main text into appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original attack evaluations on image and tabular datasets, a toy regression experiment, robustness tests and Laplace-approximation ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds text-dataset evaluations, multi-reference experiments, alternative Bayesian-method comparisons and distribution diagnostics.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 changes the test-statistic denominator from sigma/sqrt(N) to sigma*sqrt(1+1/M), explicitly accounting for target-score variability. v2 also introduces MR-BMIA: multiple reference-model posteriors, separate intra/inter-model variance estimates and a Welch-Satterthwaite degrees-of-freedom approximation (Algorithm 2; Appendix C). These change the inference procedure substantially.

E1.justification: v2 adds five text-classification datasets: Emotion, TREC-6, 20 Newsgroups, DBpedia and AG News. It also evaluates references trained on CINIC-10 against CIFAR-10 targets, a distinct distribution-mismatch scenario from the retained experiment using CINIC-10 only for non-member queries. Original image, tabular and toy-regression coverage remains.

E2.justification: v2 Table 5 newly compares BatchEnsemble, Packed Ensemble, Masksembles, SWAG and MC Dropout with Laplace-based BMIA. Table 4 adds Attack-R, LiRA and RMIA to an architecture-mismatch evaluation previously showing only BMIA. Conversely, QMIA's Texas-100, Purchase-100 and ImageNet comparisons disappear; its CIFAR results remain in Table 2.

E3.justification: v2 introduces 64-reference comparisons, reference-count scaling through K=128, single-reference RMIA comparisons, and text evaluation using BERT, DistilBERT and TF-IDF/MLP models. The stated image/tabular weight decay changes from 0.0001 in v1 Appendix B to 0.0005 in v2 Section 4.1; this establishes a reported setting revision, not that experiments were rerun. The original dataset split proportions remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New analyses test alternative Bayesian approximations, reference-count scaling, reference-training distribution shift, and Gaussian assumptions through score histograms, QQ-plots and t-statistic distributions. Architecture-mismatch analysis gains baseline comparisons. The original sampling-size, Hessian, prior-tuning and predictive-distribution ablations remain, with several relocated or renumbered.

E5.justification: v2 Table 9 newly reports means and standard deviations across reference models trained on distinct data subsets. For example, CIFAR-10 TPR at 1% FPR is reported as mean 9.48% and standard deviation 0.63 percentage points. v1 lacks this variability reporting; v2 still does not specify the run count or seeds.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive text, multi-reference and supplementary results. Table 1 revises BMIA's CIFAR-10 TPRs from 2.28/8.87 to 2.84/9.48 at 0.1%/1% FPR, and RMIA with two references changes from 8.39 to 12.86 at 1% FPR on CIFAR-100. Several training-time entries also change. Table 3 newly reports MR-BMIA TPRs of 12.48% and 45.57% at 1% FPR on CIFAR-10/100. Changed methods/settings prevent interpreting these revisions as controlled before-and-after performance gains.

T1.justification: v2 adds the intra/inter-model variance decomposition, Proposition 3.1, power-monotonicity Theorem 3.2 and their proofs, a linear-regression comparison of posterior sampling and retraining, and multi-reference variance estimators. Existing conditional-attack propositions move to Appendix B; the conditional-TPR statement changes its quantile-term sign to agree with the retained proof. The single-reference test-variance derivation is also revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion add variance reduction as a central theoretical contribution and MR-BMIA as an implemented extension benefiting from additional references. Validation claims expand to text datasets. The introductory example is corrected from 37.5% TPR and a 64% improvement on CIFAR-10 to 35.75% and 54% on CIFAR-100, consistent with Table 1.

C2.justification: v2 explains the different roles of posterior sampling and independent reference datasets, including persistent variation between model centers and diminishing returns from more references. v1's abundant-resource limitation and mixture-Laplace future work become an evaluated extension. Appendix F adds substantive warnings about non-Gaussian p-value calibration, suggests unevaluated held-out calibration, and distinguishes empirical attack power from mechanism-level privacy guarantees.

D1.justification: v2 adds a BMIA implementation-code link, PyTorch and RTX 4090/L40 hardware disclosures, and detailed storage/scalability accounting. However, v1 Appendix B's epoch budgets, learning-rate decay schedules, MLP layer widths and explicit RMIA population-set assignment are omitted rather than relocated. Most Laplace implementation details survive in Appendix G. These additions and removals substantially alter the available reproducibility information.

R1.justification: v2 expands recent MIA coverage, including recommender-system attacks, and substantially rewrites Bayesian-method positioning around post-hoc Laplace versus SWAG, MC Dropout and efficient ensembles. This replaces much of v1's variational-inference/MCMC overview. New discussions also connect the method to mixture Laplace approximations and hypothesis-testing privacy frameworks.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled and substantially rewrites its abstract, introduction, background and method exposition. The former motivation and conditional-attack theory move into appendices, while discussion material becomes structured ablation and robustness subsections. The narrative is reorganized around Bayesian sampling, variance reduction and the multi-reference extension.

P2.justification: v2 adds multiple comparison/result tables, normality diagnostics, a t-statistic plot and a log-scale ROC plot. v1's OOD table becomes Figure 2b with only two FPR thresholds, and its architecture-mismatch plot becomes Figure 2c. Existing toy and conditional-distribution illustrations move into appendices; retained Laplace-ablation plots are relaid out.

improvement.justification: v2 turns v1's multi-reference future-work limitation into a specified, evaluated method (Algorithm 2; Tables 3 and 7), accounts for target-score variance, and adds comparisons and diagnostics that directly test methodological choices and assumptions. These substantially strengthen the work's scope and evidential support. The gains outweigh omitted training schedules and an overbroad Theorem 3.2 statement: its proof requires alpha < 0.5 although the theorem claims alpha in (0,1).
